name: Food enzymes
aliases: enzymes, food enzymes, rennet, pepsin, amylase, lactase, lipase, proteases, enzimas
what_is: Proteins used to speed up specific reactions during food manufacturing. Many are used as processing aids and may be removed, inactivated or remain only as residues in the finished food.
why_botia: Food enzymes do their work during manufacturing and are often destroyed, inactivated or remain only as residues — which is why many do not appear on the ingredient list. Rennet in cheese is the best-known example: it can come from the stomach of a calf, from microorganisms, or be produced by fermentation with genetically modified microorganisms, and the label rarely makes that clear. When enzymes are declared, the name often does not reveal their source.
can_1: Detect rennet, enzymes and specific enzyme names when they are actually declared on the ingredient list.
can_2: Explain that declared enzymes may have animal, microbial, plant or fermentation-derived sources and activate the Animal and Muslim traceability layers when the source matters.
cannot_1: Detect an enzyme used as a processing aid when it does not appear anywhere on the product label.
cannot_2: Determine the exact source of a declared enzyme when the manufacturer gives only the enzyme name and no source information.

sources.label: EU Regulation 1169/2011 — ingredients and processing aids
OIC/SMIIC 24:2020 — food additives, processing aids and enzymes

title: Food enzymes
description: Food enzymes often act during manufacturing and may be absent from the ingredient list when used as processing aids. Rennet can have animal, microbial or fermentation-derived sources that the label may not reveal.
